claims.text: The book is built on documents obtained by Citizens Against UFO Secrecy under FOIA from the CIA, FBI, NSA, Air Force, NORAD and the Office of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, reproduced in facsimile and annotated.
The title derives from a Loring AFB teletype reporting that an unidentified object 'demonstrated a clear intent in the weapons storage area', a phrase the Air Force never explained.
The book was reissued in 1992 as 'The UFO Cover-Up: What the Government Won't Say', with the title page verso noting 'Originally published as Clear intent.'

connections.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
connections.note: The two bodies of work are contemporaneous and methodologically opposite: 'Clear Intent' sources every claim to a released government document, the Status Reports to protected anonymous informants. Reasoning: the difference in grade this board assigns them is entirely a difference in sourcing, not in subject matter.

desc: Fawcett and Greenwood's 1984 book is the methodological antithesis of the Stringfield corpus and the reason the nuclear-incursion strand is gradeable at tier 1. Where the crash-retrieval literature ran on anonymous testimony, 'Clear Intent' ran on Freedom of Information Act returns: CIA, FBI, NSA, Air Force, NORAD and Joint Chiefs of Staff documents obtained by Citizens Against UFO Secrecy, reproduced and annotated. Its title comes from the Loring AFB teletype reporting an object that 'demonstrated a clear intent in the weapons storage area', and its core chapters reconstruct the October-November 1975 northern-tier overflights from the NORAD Command Director's and 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's logs and the National Military Command Center memoranda, alongside the CAUS FOIA correspondence showing how those twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents were pried loose between December 1977 and February 1978. The book was reissued in 1992 as 'The UFO Cover-Up: What the Government Won't Say'. Barry Greenwood went on to direct CAUS and to edit 'Just Cause'. For this board's purposes 'Clear Intent' is the template: it demonstrates that a specific, dated, named-installation claim about unexplained aerial activity at nuclear facilities can be sourced entirely to government paper, and it thereby sets the standard that the retrieval literature has never met.
